cases.purpose: sysctl as root: dotted, slash and multiple key reads of deterministic keys; -n and -N; an unknown key with and without -e; -a with -r patterns (with and without -N); -w and implicit KEY=VALUE writes of net.ipv4 keys and kernel.domainname with read-back, -q; unknown-key writes with and without -e; a write to read-only kernel.ostype; a write as uid 2000. The same keys in the initial namespaces are shown unchanged.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: one line per invocation with its status, stdout and the diagnostic minus any "NAME: line N: " shell-location prefix; /proc/sys values after each write. Each side has fresh network and UTS namespaces, so writes to net.* keys and kernel.domainname change only that side; the initial-namespace values are read with nsenter before and after.
cases.script:
strip() { /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //' "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; }
show() { printf '%s status=%s out=' "$1" "$2"; /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < /tmp/rf.out; printf ' err='; strip /tmp/rf.err; echo; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$l" $?; }
u() { local g=--clear-groups; [[ $3 ]] && g=--groups=$3
  /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=2000 --regid=2000 $g -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
cd /tmp; K="net.ipv4.ip_forward net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding kernel.domainname"
v() { local k; for k; do printf '  %s=%s\n' $k "$(< /proc/sys/${k//.//})"; done; }
init() { [[ $(/usr/bin/readlink /proc/1/ns/net) != $(/usr/bin/readlink /proc/self/ns/net) ]] && echo "  initial namespaces distinct: yes" || echo "  initial namespaces distinct: no"
  local k; for k in $K; do printf '  init %s=%s\n' $k "$(/usr/bin/nsenter -t 1 -n -u /usr/bin/cat /proc/sys/${k//.//})"; done; }
init; v $K
r read sysctl kernel.ostype
r read-slash sysctl kernel/ostype
r read-multi sysctl kernel.ostype net.ipv4.ip_forward net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding
r value-only sysctl -n kernel.ostype net.ipv4.ip_forward
r name-only sysctl -N kernel.ostype net.ipv4.ip_forward
r unknown sysctl rf.no.such
r unknown-ignored sysctl -e rf.no.such
r unknown-among sysctl kernel.ostype rf.no.such net.ipv4.ip_forward
r pattern sysctl -a -r '^net\.ipv4\.conf\.lo\.(forwarding|rp_filter|arp_ignore)$'
r pattern-names sysctl -a -N -r '^net\.ipv4\.conf\.lo\.(forwarding|rp_filter)$'
r pattern-pattern sysctl -a --pattern '^kernel\.(ostype|domainname)$'
r write sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1; v net.ipv4.ip_forward
r write-implicit sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward=0; v net.ipv4.ip_forward
r write-quiet sysctl -q -w net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding=1; v net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding
r write-uts sysctl -w kernel.domainname=rf.example; v kernel.domainname
r write-multi sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 kernel.domainname=rf.second; v net.ipv4.ip_forward kernel.domainname
r write-spaces sysctl -w 'net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding = 0'; v net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding
r write-unknown sysctl -w rf.no.such=1
r write-unknown-ignored sysctl -e -w rf.no.such=1
r write-readonly sysctl -w kernel.ostype=Other; v kernel.ostype
u write-unprivileged "sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0"; v net.ipv4.ip_forward
r write-noequals sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward
init

cases.purpose: sysctl -p on fixture files (comments with # and ;, blank lines, spaces around =, a leading - ignore-failure prefix, an unknown key, a line without =), -p with several files and -p with no file named (/etc/sysctl.conf); --system over fixture directories bind-mounted on /etc/sysctl.d, /run/sysctl.d, /usr/lib/sysctl.d and /etc/sysctl.conf, where a same-named file in /etc/sysctl.d overrides /usr/lib/sysctl.d. Only net.ipv4 keys and kernel.domainname are set. Any missing configuration path (the guest lacks /etc/sysctl.conf and /run/sysctl.d) is created as an empty mount point for the side and removed afterwards; a same-named file in /run/sysctl.d overrides /usr/lib/sysctl.d and /usr/local/lib/sysctl.d holds its own file; if any fixture mount fails, --system is not run.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: one line per invocation with its status, stdout and the diagnostic minus any "NAME: line N: " shell-location prefix; /proc/sys values after each load. Each side has fresh network and UTS namespaces, so writes to net.* keys and kernel.domainname change only that side; the initial-namespace values are read with nsenter before and after. The system configuration paths are replaced in the side's mount namespace only.
cases.script:
strip() { /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //' "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; }
show() { printf '%s status=%s out=' "$1" "$2"; /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < /tmp/rf.out; printf ' err='; strip /tmp/rf.err; echo; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$l" $?; }
u() { local g=--clear-groups; [[ $3 ]] && g=--groups=$3
  /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=2000 --regid=2000 $g -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
cd /tmp; K="net.ipv4.ip_forward net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding kernel.domainname"
v() { local k; for k; do printf '  %s=%s\n' $k "$(< /proc/sys/${k//.//})"; done; }
init() { [[ $(/usr/bin/readlink /proc/1/ns/net) != $(/usr/bin/readlink /proc/self/ns/net) ]] && echo "  initial namespaces distinct: yes" || echo "  initial namespaces distinct: no"
  local k; for k in $K; do printf '  init %s=%s\n' $k "$(/usr/bin/nsenter -t 1 -n -u /usr/bin/cat /proc/sys/${k//.//})"; done; }
init; v $K
printf '# comment\n; also a comment\n\nnet.ipv4.ip_forward = 1\n  net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding=1\n-rf.no.such = 3\nkernel.domainname = rf.loaded\n' > /tmp/a.conf
printf 'net.ipv4.ip_forward=0\nrf.no.such = 1\nthis line has no equals\nkernel.domainname=rf.bad\n' > /tmp/bad.conf
printf 'net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding = 1\n' > /tmp/c.conf
r load sysctl -p /tmp/a.conf; v $K
r load-bad sysctl -p /tmp/bad.conf; v $K
r load-two sysctl -p /tmp/c.conf -p /tmp/a.conf; v $K
r load-missing sysctl -p /tmp/missing.conf
r load-quiet sysctl -q -p /tmp/a.conf
S=/tmp/sys; ok=1; made=
for d in /etc/sysctl.d /run/sysctl.d /usr/lib/sysctl.d /usr/local/lib/sysctl.d; do
  [[ -d $d ]] || { /usr/bin/mkdir $d && made+=" $d"; } || ok=0
  /usr/bin/mkdir -p $S$d && /usr/bin/mount --bind $S$d $d || ok=0; done
[[ -e /etc/sysctl.conf ]] || { : > /etc/sysctl.conf && made+=" /etc/sysctl.conf"; }
printf 'net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0\n' > $S/sysctl.conf && /usr/bin/mount --bind $S/sysctl.conf /etc/sysctl.conf || ok=0
if ((ok)); then
  printf 'net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1\nkernel.domainname = from-usr-lib\n' > /usr/lib/sysctl.d/10-rf.conf
  printf 'net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding = 0\n' > /usr/lib/sysctl.d/30-rf.conf
  printf 'kernel.domainname = from-etc\n' > /etc/sysctl.d/10-rf.conf
  printf 'net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding = 0\n' > /run/sysctl.d/20-rf.conf
  printf 'net.ipv4.conf.lo.forwarding = 1\n' > /run/sysctl.d/30-rf.conf
  printf 'net.ipv4.conf.default.forwarding = 1\n' > /usr/local/lib/sysctl.d/40-rf.conf
  r load-default sysctl -p; v $K; r system sysctl --system; v $K net.ipv4.conf.default.forwarding; else echo SETUP-FAILED; fi
/usr/bin/umount /etc/sysctl.conf /etc/sysctl.d /run/sysctl.d /usr/lib/sysctl.d /usr/local/lib/sysctl.d 2>/dev/null
for m in $made; do /usr/bin/rm -d -- $m; done
init

cases.purpose: sysctl -a, -A, -a -N, -a -n and -a -r on a fixed tree mounted over /proc/sys in the side's mount namespace (nested directories, a multi-word value, a multi-line value, an empty file and a write-only 0200 entry), run without CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE so the write-only entry is unreadable; then a named read of the write-only key.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: one line per invocation with its status, stdout and the diagnostic minus any "NAME: line N: " shell-location prefix. The tree is a tmpfs created by the fixture; the real /proc/sys returns when the side ends.
cases.script:
strip() { /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //' "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; }
show() { printf '%s status=%s out=' "$1" "$2"; /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < /tmp/rf.out; printf ' err='; strip /tmp/rf.err; echo; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$l" $?; }
u() { local g=--clear-groups; [[ $3 ]] && g=--groups=$3
  /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=2000 --regid=2000 $g -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
T=/tmp/ptree; /usr/bin/mkdir -p $T && /usr/bin/mount -t tmpfs -o size=1M rf-sys $T || echo SETUP-FAILED
cd $T && /usr/bin/mkdir -p abi kernel/random net/ipv4/conf/lo vm
echo 1 > abi/vsyscall32; echo Linux > kernel/ostype; echo 'rf.domain' > kernel/domainname
printf '4\t4\t1\t7\n' > kernel/printk; : > kernel/random/empty; printf 'line one\nline two\n' > vm/multi
echo 0 > net/ipv4/ip_forward; echo 1 > net/ipv4/conf/lo/forwarding; echo secret > kernel/wo; /usr/bin/chmod 0200 kernel/wo
cd /tmp; /usr/bin/mount --bind $T /proc/sys || echo SETUP-FAILED
N="/usr/bin/setpriv --bounding-set=-dac_override,-dac_read_search -- $BASH --noprofile --norc -c"
d() { $N "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
d all "sysctl -a"
d all-upper "sysctl -A"
d names "sysctl -a -N"
d values "sysctl -a -n"
d pattern "sysctl -a -r '^net\.'"
d pattern-names "sysctl -a -N -r 'o(stype|main)'"
d write-only "sysctl kernel.wo"
/usr/bin/umount /proc/sys; /usr/bin/umount $T

cases.purpose: dmesg reading the live /dev/kmsg ring after a util-linux clear and four seeded user-facility records (info, err, warning, notice): -f user -t, with -l err,warn, -r -t, -x -t, -k -t; -c -f user -t prints the records and clears the ring (a following read is empty); as uid 2000, reading and -c fail and the ring keeps a reseeded record; with BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE pointing at a fixture file, -c under a filter that kills syslog(2).
cases.oracle: util-linux 2.41 dmesg on the same ring; util-linux dmesg as the ring readback
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: one line per invocation with its status, stdout and the diagnostic minus any "NAME: line N: " shell-location prefix; the user-facility ring contents read by util-linux after each clearing step. Timestamps are suppressed with -t. The ring is shared by both sides, so each side clears and reseeds it first.
cases.script:
strip() { /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //' "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; }
show() { printf '%s status=%s out=' "$1" "$2"; /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < /tmp/rf.out; printf ' err='; strip /tmp/rf.err; echo; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$l" $?; }
u() { local g=--clear-groups; [[ $3 ]] && g=--groups=$3
  /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=2000 --regid=2000 $g -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
lvl=$(/usr/bin/cut -f1 /proc/sys/kernel/printk)
trap 'echo $lvl > /proc/sys/kernel/printk' EXIT
seed() { local m; for m; do printf '%s\n' "$m" > /dev/kmsg; done; }
ring() { echo "  ring: $(/usr/bin/dmesg -f user -t | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|')"; }
/usr/bin/dmesg -C || echo SETUP-FAILED
seed '<14>rf-seed: info record one' '<11>rf-seed: error record two' '<12>rf-seed: warning record three' '<13>rf-seed: notice record four'
r user dmesg -f user -t
r levels dmesg -f user -t -l err,warn
r raw dmesg -f user -r -t
r decode dmesg -f user -x -t
r kernel-only dmesg -k -t -l emerg
r clear dmesg -c -f user -t; ring
r after-clear dmesg -f user -t
seed '<14>rf-seed: kept record'
u read-unprivileged "dmesg -f user -t"
u clear-unprivileged "dmesg -c"; ring
printf '6,1,100,-;rf-fixture: hook record\n' > /tmp/kmsg.txt; /usr/bin/chmod 0644 /tmp/kmsg.txt
BASHDMESG_DEV_KMSG_FILE=/tmp/kmsg.txt PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-seccomp.py --kill syslog -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'dmesg -c -t' >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show hook-clear $?; ring

cases.purpose: dmesg -n with numeric levels 1, 4 and 8, named levels (err, debug), an invalid name, an out-of-range number and a missing argument; as uid 2000, -n 4 fails and the level stays. The console level (first field of /proc/sys/kernel/printk) is shown after each step and restored when the side ends.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status, stdout and stderr: one line per invocation with its status, stdout and the diagnostic minus any "NAME: line N: " shell-location prefix; the console level after each step.
cases.script:
strip() { /usr/bin/sed -E 's/^[^:]*: line [0-9]+: //' "$1" | /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|'; }
show() { printf '%s status=%s out=' "$1" "$2"; /usr/bin/tr '\n' '|' < /tmp/rf.out; printf ' err='; strip /tmp/rf.err; echo; }
r() { local l=$1; shift; "$@" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$l" $?; }
u() { local g=--clear-groups; [[ $3 ]] && g=--groups=$3
  /usr/bin/setpriv --reuid=2000 --regid=2000 $g -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "$2" >/tmp/rf.out 2>/tmp/rf.err; show "$1" $?; }
lvl=$(/usr/bin/cut -f1 /proc/sys/kernel/printk)
trap 'echo $lvl > /proc/sys/kernel/printk' EXIT
c() { echo "  console level: $(/usr/bin/cut -f1 /proc/sys/kernel/printk)"; }
echo 7 > /proc/sys/kernel/printk; c
r n1 dmesg -n 1; c
r n4 dmesg -n 4; c
r n8 dmesg -n 8; c
r named-err dmesg -n err; c
r named-debug dmesg -n debug; c
r bad-name dmesg -n bogus; c
r out-of-range dmesg -n 9; c
r missing dmesg -n; c
echo 6 > /proc/sys/kernel/printk
u unprivileged "dmesg -n 4"; c
